records.context: A database already damaged by an earlier resume cannot be repaired on read — the rows are gone, and nothing in the file records what they were. records.context: **A file that exists is not a file that finished.** Older versions of ``spacr.io._load_and_concatenate_arrays`` wrote ``merged/<field>.npy`` with a bare ``np.save`` straight onto the destination path, so a crash mid-write left a short, structurally valid-looking ``.npy`` on disk. Current versions write merged arrays atomically, but files left by earlier runs can still be truncated. A resume that skips on ``os.path.exists`` would accept such a field, measure whatever bytes happened to land, and put the result in the same table as the good fields. So :func:`completed_fields_in_merged` *validates*: it parses the ``.npy`` header and checks that the file is as long as its own shape claims. Anything short is reported as rejected and re-queued, never skipped.
records.label: spacr.resume#3
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **A file that exists is not a file that finished.** Older versions of ``spacr.io._load_and_concatenate_arrays`` wrote ``merged/<field>.npy`` with a bare ``np.save`` straight onto the destination path, so a crash mid-write left a short, structurally valid-looking ``.npy`` on disk. Current versions write merged arrays atomically, but files left by earlier runs can still be truncated. A resume that skips on ``os.path.exists`` would accept such a field, measure whatever bytes happened to land, and put the result in the same table as the good fields. So :func:`completed_fields_in_merged` *validates*: it parses the ``.npy`` header and checks that the file is as long as its own shape claims. Anything short is reported as rejected and re-queued, never skipped.
records.translation: **Un archivo que existe no es un archivo terminado.** Las versiones anteriores de ``spacr.io._load_and_concatenate_arrays`` escribían ``merged/<field>.npy`` con un simple ``np.save`` directamente sobre la ruta de destino, de modo que un fallo a mitad de la escritura dejaba en el disco un ``.npy`` corto y de estructura aparentemente válida. Las versiones actuales escriben las matrices fusionadas de forma atómica, pero los archivos dejados por ejecuciones anteriores todavía pueden estar truncados. Una reanudación que omitiera campos según ``os.path.exists`` aceptaría un campo así, mediría los bytes que hubieran llegado a escribirse y pondría el resultado en la misma tabla que los campos correctos. Por eso :func:`completed_fields_in_merged` *valida*: analiza la cabecera del ``.npy`` y comprueba que el archivo tenga la longitud que declara su propia forma. Todo archivo corto se notifica como rechazado y se vuelve a poner en cola, nunca se omite.

records.context: **The measurement workflow appends rows, so existing rows must be removed prior to continuing an interrupted run.** ``_merge_and_save_to_database`` and ``filepaths_to_database`` both call ``to_sql(..., if_exists='append')``. Measuring a field again does not replace existing rows; it *inserts additional rows*. This makes downstream per-well aggregates too large without a warning. :func:`clear_field_rows` removes old rows so repeated measurement produces one consistent result. One transaction covers every affected table, so an error leaves the database unchanged.
records.label: spacr.resume#4
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Measure appends; therefore a resume must delete first.** ``_merge_and_save_to_database`` and ``filepaths_to_database`` both use ``to_sql(..., if_exists='append')``. Re-measuring a field that already wrote some rows does not overwrite them, it *adds* to them, and every per-well aggregate downstream is then computed over inflated counts with nothing anywhere to indicate it. :func:`clear_field_rows` is the delete-before-insert that makes re-running a field idempotent, and it is the reason this module exists at all. It runs in one transaction across every table the field touched, so a failure part-way leaves the database exactly as it was.
records.translation: **Measure añade filas; por tanto, una reanudación debe borrar primero.** ``_merge_and_save_to_database`` y ``filepaths_to_database`` usan ambas ``to_sql(..., if_exists='append')``. Volver a medir un campo que ya escribió algunas filas no las sobrescribe, sino que las *suma*, y todos los agregados por pocillo posteriores se calculan entonces sobre recuentos inflados sin que nada lo indique. :func:`clear_field_rows` es el borrado previo a la inserción que hace idempotente volver a procesar un campo, y es la razón de que este módulo exista. Se ejecuta en una sola transacción sobre todas las tablas que tocó el campo, de modo que un fallo a mitad de camino deja la base de datos exactamente como estaba.

records.context: **measurements.db is not measure's private file.** ``convert`` writes ``conversion_map`` into it, ``align`` writes ``align_coordinates``, ``foreign`` writes ``foreign_*``, ``timelapse`` writes its track table — all keyed on the same four columns as the measurements, deliberately, so that they join. Discovering "tables to clear" by their columns alone would therefore find all of them, and clearing a pending microscope field of view from each would delete the only record of which vendor file became ``plate1_A01_1``, of where each microscope image field was stitched, and of imported measurements. None of it can be recomputed from the database. The tables a resume may delete from are therefore an explicit allow-list, :data:`MEASURE_OWNED_TABLES`, checked both when the list is discovered and again per table immediately before the DELETE is prepared.
records.label: spacr.resume#5
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context

Discovering "tables to clear" by their columns alone would therefore find all of them, and clearing a pending field from each would delete the only record of which vendor file became ``plate1_A01_1``, of where each tile was stitched, and of imported measurements. None of it can be recomputed from the database. The tables a resume may delete from are therefore an explicit allow-list, :data:`MEASURE_OWNED_TABLES`, checked both when the list is discovered and again per table immediately before the DELETE is prepared.
records.translation: **measurements.db no es un archivo privado de measure.** ``convert`` escribe ``conversion_map`` en ella, ``align`` escribe ``align_coordinates``, ``foreign`` escribe ``foreign_*`` y ``timelapse`` escribe su tabla de trayectorias — todas indexadas deliberadamente por las mismas cuatro columnas que las mediciones, para que puedan combinarse. Descubrir las "tables to clear" (tablas que hay que borrar) solo por sus columnas las encontraría por tanto a todas, y borrar un campo pendiente de cada una eliminaría el único registro de qué archivo del fabricante se convirtió en ``plate1_A01_1``, de dónde se unió cada tesela y de las mediciones importadas. Nada de ello (None) puede recalcularse a partir de la base de datos. Por eso, las tablas de las que una reanudación puede borrar forman una lista explícita de permitidas, :data:`MEASURE_OWNED_TABLES`, que se comprueba tanto al descubrir la lista como de nuevo para cada tabla inmediatamente antes de preparar el DELETE.

records.context: **Owned by name is not owned in fact, so ownership is decided per row.** A name allow-list answers "could measure have written this table?", and there is one case where the answer to "did it?" is no: ``foreign.run_import`` copies the imported rows into the canonical ``cell`` / ``nucleus`` / ``pathogen`` table when nothing of anyone else's is there, so that a purely-imported project is readable by every spaCR tool. Those rows sit under spaCR's own metadata columns in a table on the allow-list, and a table-level rule would clear them along with the pending field.
records.label: spacr.resume#6

records.source: **Owned by name is not owned in fact, so ownership is decided per row.** A name allow-list answers "could measure have written this table?", and there is one case where the answer to "did it?" is no: ``foreign.run_import`` copies the imported rows into the canonical ``cell`` / ``nucleus`` / ``pathogen`` table when nothing of anyone else's is there, so that a purely-imported project is readable by every spaCR tool. Those rows sit under spaCR's own metadata columns in a table on the allow-list, and a table-level rule would clear them along with the pending field.
records.translation: **Pertenecer por nombre no es pertenecer de hecho, así que la propiedad se decide por fila.** Una lista de nombres permitidos responde a "¿podría measure haber escrito esta tabla?", y hay un caso en que la respuesta a "¿lo hizo?" es no: ``foreign.run_import`` copia las filas importadas en la tabla canónica ``cell`` / ``nucleus`` / ``pathogen`` cuando no hay en ella nada de nadie más, para que cualquier herramienta de spaCR pueda leer un proyecto puramente importado. Esas filas están bajo las columnas de metadatos propias de spaCR en una tabla de la lista de permitidas, y una regla a nivel de tabla las borraría junto con el campo pendiente.

records.context: The rows are told apart by ``foreign_columns``, written by every release of the importer, names each column that importer put in each table. Its table-scoped use — ``foreign._importer_owns``, "are this table's columns a subset of what the importer recorded?" — has a row-scoped twin, and that is the rule here: **a row is the importer's when every column it is non-NULL in is one the importer recorded for this table**. A ``measure_crop`` row always carries at least its own area and intensity columns, which the importer never wrote; an imported row carries only metadata and ``foreign_``-prefixed measurements. So a table can be half one and half the other and each row is still attributable — which matters, because a project that was imported and then measured is exactly that. See :func:`measure_rows_clause`.
records.label: spacr.resume#7

records.source: The rows are told apart by ``foreign_columns``, written by every release of the importer, names each column that importer put in each table. Its table-scoped use — ``foreign._importer_owns``, "are this table's columns a subset of what the importer recorded?" — has a row-scoped twin, and that is the rule here: **a row is the importer's when every column it is non-NULL in is one the importer recorded for this table**. A ``measure_crop`` row always carries at least its own area and intensity columns, which the importer never wrote; an imported row carries only metadata and ``foreign_``-prefixed measurements. So a table can be half one and half the other and each row is still attributable — which matters, because a project that was imported and then measured is exactly that. See :func:`measure_rows_clause`.
records.translation: Las filas se distinguen mediante ``foreign_columns``, que todas las versiones del importador escriben y que nombra cada columna que el importador puso en cada tabla. Su uso a nivel de tabla — ``foreign._importer_owns``, "¿son las columnas de esta tabla un subconjunto de lo que registró el importador?" — tiene un equivalente a nivel de fila, y esa es la regla aquí: **una fila pertenece al importador cuando todas las columnas en las que no es NULL son columnas que el importador registró para esta tabla**. Una fila de ``measure_crop`` siempre contiene al menos sus propias columnas de área e intensidad, que el importador nunca escribió; una fila importada solo contiene metadatos y mediciones con el prefijo ``foreign_``. Así, una tabla puede ser mitad de uno y mitad del otro y cada fila sigue siendo atribuible — lo cual importa, porque un proyecto que se importó y luego se midió es exactamente eso. Véase :func:`measure_rows_clause`.

records.context: Ownership is not read from a table-level marker such as ``foreign_import.canonical_table_written``. A marker that blocks every delete from a claimed table would also block clearing fields the import never covered, so such a project could never be resumed; and the first importer release wrote the canonical copy without that marker. ``foreign_columns`` is per table and per column, and every importer release has written it.

Un marcador que bloqueara todo borrado en una tabla reclamada también impediría borrar campos que la importación nunca cubrió, de modo que un proyecto así nunca podría reanudarse; además, la primera versión del importador escribió la copia canónica sin ese marcador. ``foreign_columns`` es por tabla y por columna, y todas las versiones del importador lo han escrito.
